implementerProof.how: Each of the implementer's five proof entries was re-run or driven independently. (1) Acceptance 1 and 2: I re-ran both lanes at the head, 0 of 50 under -race (ok 526.289s) and 0 of 50 without it (ok 524.633s), against its 529.896s and 523.528s. (2) The cause: I read the pinned server's own source in the module cache rather than taking the trace - v2.10.29 server/jetstream_cluster.go:6287-6328 locks js.mu, unlocks it for jsa.configUpdateCheck at :6305-6307, locks it again and then calls cc.subjectsOverlap at :6328, and subjectsOverlap (:560-576) skips a stream only on pointer identity (sa == osa); v2.15.1 (:1187-1202) skips by name. I then bisected the release claim: v2.11.9 and v2.12.4 skip by pointer, v2.12.5 by name, so 'every nats-server before v2.12.5' is exact. (3) The remedy, failing first: in a scratch copy of the head tree with only internal/bus/stream.go restored from the base (the two new constants declared beside it), TestConcurrentUpdatesOfOneStreamEndWithTheStreamHoldingThem failed 5 of 5 under -race (FAIL 17.508s; rounds 9, 13, 38, 157 and 184) and TestAnUpdateRefusedAsOverlappingItsOwnStreamIsSettledFromTheStream failed 4 of its 7 rows; both pass at the head, 10 of 10 under -race. (4) The hub's server: I built my own one-off clusters of three real nats-server binaries, v2.15.1 and v2.10.29, and drove the product through them. (5) The suite and CI: read at 4ff726ac on GitHub, not re-run. The implementer's base measurement of acceptance 1 (0 of 200, the escape clause the pull request quotes) is the one number I did not reproduce as written: my 20-iteration run of the acceptance-5 set at the reconstructed base caught that same test failing once, with this issue's message, so the base does fail here too, less often than the planner's 1 of 50.

proof.observed: Head: `ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/bus 1282.962s`, 0 of 20 iterations failed. Base: 8 of the 20 iterations failed - 7 on `--- FAIL: TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers drain_hook_edges_test.go:249: the drain logged "WARN envoy nats reconnect attempt failed", want nothing` (one iteration logged it three times) and 1 on TestTwoStartsRaisingOneStreamAtOnceBothSucceed. The stray records in the base run are `name=envoy` with three server URLs, a client of another test's stopped cluster, while the drain test's own server is one URL.
proof.negativeControl: The filter could have passed this test by swallowing the record it is for, so I drove the real logger: in a scratch copy of the head tree, a client connected with bus.WithName(t.Name()) through the relay proxy, the proxy then closed, logs `WARN envoy nats reconnect attempt failed` with that name, and warnOrErrorRecords keeps it (the subtest asserting it is kept passes); the same warning from a client named `another-test-client` is dropped (the subtest asserting it is dropped passes). So TestAStuckDeliveryStillEndsTheKVWatchers still fails on its own client's reconnect warning, which is the defect it guards. A second control: the base's drain tests with the head's product code failed 0 of 5 iterations of the same set, so the product fix alone already removes most of the leak's source; the test-only change is what makes the assertion independent of it.

proof.criterion: The Outcome's second server: two programs that start at the same moment both start, and the stream and every bucket end at the deployment's replica count, on nats-server v2.10.29 and on the hub's v2.15.1 (architect decision 4).
proof.surface: One-off clusters of three real nats-server binaries on loopback, v2.15.1 and v2.10.29, each with its own JetStream store, built and started by me under $TMPDIR and stopped after the run; the product driven through ConnectOwningStream and EnsureKeyValue from a throwaway test that takes the cluster's URLs from the environment.
proof.command: `bash $TMPDIR/infra750/oneoff.sh v2.15.1` and `... v2.10.29`: `GOBIN=$TMPDIR/infra750/bin go install github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@<version>`, three configs sharing one cluster route, then `PROBE_CLUSTER_URLS=<three URLs> go test -count=1 -timeout 15m -v -run 'TestProbeOneOffOnARealCluster$' ./internal/bus/` in a copy of the head tree.
proof.observed: v2.15.1 (`nats-server: v2.15.1`): both starts succeeded, ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS and KV_envoy_probe_oneoff each at three copies, and 0 overlap refusals in 900 raw concurrent updates - `PROBE RESULT: 0 overlap refusals and 0 other failures in 900 raw updates`, PASS 4.76s. v2.10.29 (`nats-server: v2.10.29`): both starts succeeded and both streams reached three copies at the head, while the raw measurement caught `PROBE RESULT: 2 overlap refusals and 0 other failures in 900 raw updates`, PASS 17.04s.
proof.negativeControl: The same 900-update measurement on the two versions is the control for itself: 2 refusals on v2.10.29 against 0 on v2.15.1, so the v2.15.1 zero is the server's fix and not a probe that cannot see a refusal. The source bisect holds the same way: v2.11.9 and v2.12.4 skip the stream by pointer identity (`if osa != nil && sa == osa`), v2.12.5 and v2.15.1 by name (`sa.Config.Name == osa.Config.Name`).

notes: Not a failure, a prose finding for the reviewer, which the reviewer fixes in its own commit: the pull request's title, 'fix(envoy): a start that meets another start's stream or bucket mid-create no longer fails', names the create path, which this change does not touch - the implementer's own trace found no create-path refusal in 240 starts and left ensureStreamWithConfig's and EnsureKeyValue's create branches exactly as they were. With this repository's squash settings that title becomes main's commit subject and the release note, so it would record a fix that was not made. The branch's own commit subject, 'fix(envoy): a stream update refused as overlapping its own stream is sent again', is accurate.

A property of the fix that is unchanged by it, recorded so the reviewer need not re-derive it: an overlap-refused update is sent again as the caller built it, from the stream the caller read before the refusal, so a concurrent write that does not satisfy this caller (another program's larger ENVOY_STREAM_MAX_BYTES with fewer replicas, or a different build's subject list) can be overwritten by the re-send. That is the write a server without the race takes after the other update: the same loss happens on v2.12.5 and later, where the first send is accepted, and the loop re-sends only while the stream, read again, does not already hold what this caller asked for (ensureStreamWithConfig's holds is reconciledStream(again, cfg) == again.Config, stream.go:434-437). So the change widens no window that ownedStream's never-lower rule did not already leave open.
